overview.text: Christ Pantocrator presents Christ as the Almighty. Thomas Hopko’s explanation of church imagery places Christ the Almighty at the centre of the building, within a wider programme of images of the Church and Kingdom.

blocks.text: The displayed Sinai icon shows Christ facing the viewer, with a cross-marked halo, a hand raised in blessing, and a richly covered Gospel book. It is a single frontal portrait rather than a narrative scene.

blocks.text: The image catalogue identifies this as the sixth-century encaustic Christ Pantocrator of Saint Catherine’s Monastery at Sinai. Its material and date belong to this particular surviving work, rather than to every later icon bearing the same title.

blocks.text: Hopko connects the possibility of depicting Christ with the Incarnation: the Word truly became human. His catechesis treats icons as witnesses to God’s presence and the Kingdom, with John 1:14 among its explicit scriptural foundations.
